Gauss-Hermite rule for the standard normal

Source: R/agq.R
tulpa_gauss_hermite.Rd

Nodes and weights of the n-point Gauss-Hermite rule for the probabilists' weight, normalised to the standard normal density, so that sum(weights * f(nodes)) approximates E[f(Z)] for Z ~ N(0, 1) and is exact for polynomials of degree up to 2n - 1. Computed by Golub-Welsch: the nodes are the eigenvalues of the symmetric tridiagonal Jacobi matrix of the probabilists' Hermite recurrence (zero diagonal, off-diagonal sqrt(k)), the weights the squared first components of its eigenvectors. A normal N(m, s^2) is integrated at m + s * nodes with the same weights.

Usage

tulpa_gauss_hermite(n)

Arguments

n

Number of nodes (a positive integer).

Value

A list with nodes (increasing) and weights (summing to one), each of length n.

See also

tulpa_re_aghq(), tulpa_latent_ascent()

Examples

gh <- tulpa_gauss_hermite(5)
sum(gh$weights * gh$nodes^4)   # E[Z^4] = 3
#> [1] 3
